title: API key fallback loop during token refresh + leader change causing intermittent org misassignment
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments have reported intermittent authorization failures where valid API requests are rejected or attributed to the wrong org after leader-election events and token refresh cycles. Symptoms include 401s followed by a short window where requests are accepted but resolved to a different org ID, triggering cross-tenant access alerts. The issue escalated from support cases with two enterprise Dedicated customers and one Private deployment. Impact is production-facing, intermittent (~0.1-0.5% of requests during leader-change windows) and correlated with token refresh and edge leader handoff paths.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure dedicated pool with multi-zone leader election enabled and short session TTL (e.g., 60s)
2) Issue API key auth requests concurrently from two org-scoped clients (OrgA and OrgB) with rapid token refresh enabled on the client side
3) Trigger a leader handoff (simulate controller restart or zone failover) while refreshes are in-flight

4) Observe authorization logs: some refresh completion callbacks are applied to the pre-handoff in-memory session map, while routing points to the new leader's cache, causing a fallback path that binds the refresh result to a namespace default and then to the wrong org
5) Result: transient 401s during the handoff followed by accepted requests that are resolved under incorrect org context until next token rotation/explicit session invalidation
recent_comments: 2026-03-02 Diego Morales: Reproduced in staging with race on refresh callback + leader-change. Captured logs and correlation IDs. Attaching traces to GH issue.
2026-03-04 SRE Lead (Marta Chen): Temporary mitigation applied at edge: hold leader-change for 30s if in-flight refreshes detected. Reduced customer reports but not a long-term solution.
2026-03-07 Support (Noah Patel): Customer A confirmed that manual session invalidation cleared the misassigned sessions. Provided customer-facing mitigation steps.

2026-03-10 Aisha Kumar: Root cause analysis in progress — working theory: non-atomic refresh write to multi-tier cache during leader election; fallback path uses namespace fallback which is non-deterministic under race. Preparing patch to serialize refresh writes per apikey-session-id.
mitigation_actions: Rollback recent cache sharding changes that widened leader resiliency surface (deployed as emergency rollback 2026-03-03)
Edge hold: SRE deploys a 30s hold during leader transition if active refreshes > 0, reducing observed window
Customer mitigation doc: steps to force full session rotation and temporary increase of refresh interval to avoid concurrent refreshes during cutovers
Support playbook updated with correlation IDs and how to trigger manual session invalidation for affected customers
root_cause_summary: During leader-election and controller failover, token refresh completion handlers wrote updated session state into a per-leader in-memory cache without global atomic coordination. The new leader attempted to reconcile in-flight refreshes by calling a fallback path that applied namespace default bindings when session ownership lookup failed. A timing window allowed the fallback to write an org-scoped binding that belonged to a different refresh in the queue, producing transient org misassignment until cached values rotated out.
fix_description: 1) Introduce a per-apikey-session mutex/serial queue keyed by apikey-session-id so refresh completion writes are serialized across leader transitions. 2) Change fallback behavior: if session ownership lookup fails during leader-change, avoid writing default org bindings and instead return a transient 503 to trigger client retry until ownership is resolved. 3) Add a short-lived global refresh tombstone in distributed cache so new leader knows in-flight refreshes exist and blocks fallback writes for that key. 4) Add end-to-end tests simulating leader handoff + refresh storms.
deployment_plan: Stage patch to canary hosts in staging cluster (2026-03-11)
Run chaos test: orchestrate leader election while issuing refresh-heavy workload for 30m
If green, promote to controlled canary on one Dedicated customer cluster during their maintenance window (2026-03-13)
Monitor metrics: auth 4xx rate, org-binding mismatches, session tombstone hits, errors returned as 503 for fallback paths
Progressive rollout to Hosted/Private with 2-hour observation windows per shard, auto-roll-back on anomaly threshold
validation_checklist: Unit tests for per-session mutex and fallback guard
Integration test that asserts no org rebinds during simulated leader elections
Load test with refresh storm (1000 concurrent refreshes) to validate mutex scaling characteristics
Canary monitoring dashboards with alerts for org-resolve-errors and 503 fallback spikes
Security review sign-off on tombstone behavior and race mitigation (required)
postmortem_next_steps: Create confluence postmortem with timeline and customer impact (owner: Aisha)
Add permanent metric 'in-flight-refreshes' and SLO boundary to avoid future hot-path leader-handoff storms
Design long-term: replace per-leader in-memory session with sharded CRDT-backed session map to tolerate handoffs without tombstones
Customer outreach: notify affected customers, include mitigation steps and planned fix ETA
Backfill regression tests into CI so future cache sharding changes run leader-election + refresh smoke tests
